319712.title: The Weak Anti-Freiman conjecture
319712.literal_statement:
Let $A \subseteq \mathbb Z$ be a finite set. For every subset $A' \subseteq A$, suppose that

$$
|A'+A'|\geq \delta |A'|^2 \quad\text{and}\quad |A'-A'|\geq \delta |A'|^2.
$$

Here, a $B_2[g]$ set is a set in which every integer has at most $g$ representations as a sum of two elements, and a $B^\circ_2[g]$ set is a set in which every nonzero integer has at most $g$ representations as a difference of two elements.

**Weak Anti-Freiman conjecture.** Then $A$ contains either a $B_2[g]$ set or a $B^\circ_2[g]$ set of size at least $\delta'|A|$, where $g$ and $\delta'$ depend only on $\delta$.

The conjecture is presented as a weaker version of an anti-Freiman question, but the paper states immediately afterward that it is false and constructs counterexamples.

319992.title: Bang-Jensen, Gutin and Li's dominated-pair conjecture
319992.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a strongly connected digraph on $n\geq 2$ vertices. For vertices $x,y$, let $d(x)$ denote total degree, and call a pair dominated if some vertex sends an edge to both vertices.

**Bang-Jensen, Gutin and Li's conjecture.** If $d(x)+d(y)\geq 2n-1$ for every dominated pair of non-adjacent vertices in $G$, then $G$ has a Hamilton cycle.

This would strengthen Meyniel's theorem by imposing the degree condition only on dominated pairs of non-adjacent vertices. The supplied text gives no resolution status.

320085.title: Critical-threshold conjecture for the splitting model
320085.literal_statement:
Let the splitting model on $\mathbb Z^d$ have parameter $h$, and let robust and explosive denote its two regimes.

**Critical-threshold conjecture.** There exists a critical value $h_c=h_c(d)$ such that, for all $h<h_c$, the model is robust, while for all $h\geq h_c$, the model is explosive. Moreover,

$$
\nh_c(2)=\frac{2}{3}.
$$

The conjecture proposes that the robust and explosive behaviors are separated by a single threshold, independent of the splitting order. The value $h_c(2)=2/3$ is suggested by simulations, while the behavior in the intermediate parameter range is not established by the paper.

320190.title: Conjecture on eventual completion of simple partial multi-latin squares
320190.literal_statement: Let $k$ and $m$ be positive integers. A **simple** partial $k$-latin square is a partial $k$-latin square in which no symbol is repeated within a cell. **Eventual embedding conjecture.** There exists a finite value $n(m,k)$ such that, for every $n\geq n(m,k)$, every simple partial $k$-latin square $P$ of order $m$ embeds in a simple $k$-latin square of order $n$. The preceding theorem establishes the analogous embedding result without the simplicity requirement; determining whether simplicity can also be preserved remains open.

320241.title: Disk minimality conjecture for sums of Dirichlet eigenvalues
320241.literal_statement: Let $\Omega$ be a bounded plane domain of diameter $D$, and let $0<\lambda_1\leq\lambda_2\leq\cdots$ be the Dirichlet eigenvalues of its Laplacian. **Disk eigenvalue-sum conjecture.** For every $n\geq1$, the quantity $(\lambda_1+\cdots+\lambda_n)D^2$ is minimal when $\Omega$ is a disk. The case $n=1$ follows from the Faber--Krahn and isodiametric theorems, while the general assertion remains open.

320294.title: Dimension formula conjecture for multilinear right-commutative monomials
320294.literal_statement:
Let $FRC_n$ be the multilinear subspace of degree $n$ in the free right-commutative algebra on $n$ generators. An ordered basis of $FRC_n$ consists of the distinct right-commutative monomials in degree $n$, ordered first by association type and then lexicographically by the underlying permutation. For all $n\geq 1$, **the dimension formula conjecture.**

$$
\dim FRC_n \stackrel{?}{=} \frac{n(2n{-}2)!}{2^{n-1}(n{-}1)!}.
$$

The formula is motivated by computed dimensions for $1\leq n\leq 9$ and agrees with the cited Sloane sequence A001193. Its status is not established in the supplied source.

320412.title: Conjecture on Fibonacci-numeration P-positions of Wythoff star
320412.literal_statement:
Let $F_n$ denote the Fibonacci numbers, and let $(A_i,B_i)$ be the pairs occurring in Theorem 2. For all $ne 3$ and every $i$ such that the stated inequalities hold, the following positions are $P$-positions:

$$
A_i+B_i\le F_{2n-4}
$$

implies

$$
(F_{2n-1},F_{2n}-1-A_i-B_i),
$$

and

$$
A_i\le F_{2n-4}
$$

implies

$$
(F_{2n-1}+A_i,F_{2n}-1).
$$

**Conjecture on Fibonacci-numeration P-positions.** For all $n\ge 3$ and all $i$ satisfying these conditions, both displayed positions are $P$-positions of the game under consideration. This would extend the preceding characterization of Wythoff-star positions by similar methods; the source provides no resolution.

320418.title: The finite-or-continuum conjecture for minimal coloring counts
320418.literal_statement:
A finite system $\mathcal{L}$ of linear homogeneous equations over $\mathbb{Q}$ is called **nonregular** if it is not regular over $\mathbb{Q}$. Let $\Delta(\mathcal{L};\mathbb{Q})$ denote the number of minimal colorings, up to isomorphism, of the nonzero rational numbers.

**The finite-or-continuum conjecture.** For every nonregular finite system $\mathcal{L}$ of linear homogeneous equations, either $\Delta(\mathcal{L};\mathbb{Q})$ is finite or $2^{\aleph_0}$. In particular, there is no $\mathcal{L}$ satisfying

$$
\Delta(\mathcal{L};\mathbb{Q})=\aleph_0.
$$

The paper establishes examples with finitely many and with $2^{\aleph_0}$ minimal colorings, including the equation $x_1+x_2+x_3=4x_4$. Whether countably infinite values can occur remains open.

320749.title: Kapovich–Weidmann conjecture on higher stabilization for Nielsen equivalence
320749.literal_statement:
Let $k\ge m\ge 2$, and let

$$
G=\langle a_1,\ldots,a_k,b_1,\ldots,b_m\mid a_i=u_i(\bar b),\ b_j=v_j(\bar a)\text{ for }1\le i\le k,\ 1\le j\le m\rangle.
$$

Assume the tuples of defining words lie in the generic subsets specified in the construction and satisfy $|u_1|=|v_1|$.

**Kapovich–Weidmann higher-stabilization conjecture.** For every $1\le t<m$, the generating $(k+t)$-tuple $(a_1,\ldots,a_k,1,\ldots,1)$ is not equivalent to a $(k+t)$-tuple of type $(b_1,\ldots,b_{t+1},g_1,\ldots,g_{k-1})$.

This strengthens the preceding one-stabilization obstruction: fewer than $m$ stabilizations should not suffice to relate the generating tuples. The notation for the generic subsets and the precise equivalence relation is inherited from the surrounding construction.

342515.title: Shalev's Engel word-map conjecture
342515.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple non-abelian group, and let $n\geq 1$. The $n$-th Engel word is the word $e_n=[y,[y,\ldots,[y,x]\ldots]]$ with $y$ occurring $n$ times, and its word map is

$$
G\times G\longrightarrow G.
$$

**Shalev's conjecture.** For every finite simple non-abelian group $G$ and every $n\geq 1$, the $n$-th Engel word map

$$
G\times G\longrightarrow G
$$

is surjective.

The conjecture extends the Ore conjecture from the commutator word to all Engel words. The supplied source gives no resolution status for Shalev's conjecture.

345575.title: Global rigidity conjecture for graphs containing triangulations of surfaces
345575.literal_statement: Let $G$ be a graph with a triangulation $T$ of a surface $S$ as a spanning subgraph. A graph is **globally rigid** when its generic realization is uniquely determined, up to Euclidean isometry, by its edge lengths. **Global rigidity conjecture for triangulated surfaces.** The graph $G$ is globally rigid if and only if $G$ is $4$-connected and, when $S$ has genus zero, $G\neq T$. The conjecture extends the planar triangulation result to arbitrary surfaces. It appeared previously as a question and has been verified when $S$ is the sphere, projective plane, or torus; the general case remains open.

381077.title: The product conjecture for finite transitive sets in Euclidean Ramsey theory
381077.literal_statement:
Let $X\subset\mathbb{R}^m$ be a finite transitive set. A set $Y\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ is **$k$-Ramsey for $X$** if every $k$-colouring of $Y$ contains a subset congruent to $X$. For a positive integer $n$, regard $X^n$ as a subset of $\mathbb{R}^{mn}$, and call $\lambda X^n=\{\lambda x:x\in X^n\}$ a scaling of $X^n$.

**The product conjecture.** For every positive integer $k$, there exists a positive integer $n$ such that some scaling of $X^n$ is $k$-Ramsey for $X$.

This strengthens the usual approach to proving that sets are Ramsey, in which a finite transitive set is embedded and then a large product is coloured. The conjecture is presented as the geometric statement later reformulated in purely combinatorial terms; its resolution is not specified in the supplied text.

318243.title: Generalized Dipper–James–Murphy conjecture for Kleshchev multipartitions
318243.literal_statement: Let $\mathcal{P}_r(n)$ be the set of $r$-partitions of $n$, let $\mathcal{K}_r(n)$ be the set of Kleshchev $r$-partitions with respect to $(e;\mathbf{Q})$, and let an $r$-partition be $(\mathbf{Q},e)$-restricted if it admits a standard tableau whose residue sequence is distinct from the residue sequence of every standard tableau of every strictly smaller multipartition. **Generalized Dipper–James–Murphy conjecture.** For every $\boldsymbol\lambda\in\mathcal{P}_r(n)$, $\boldsymbol\lambda\in\mathcal{K}_r(n)$ if and only if $\boldsymbol\lambda$ is $(\mathbf{Q},e)$-restricted. The equivalence is known for $r=1$ and $r=2$, while the general case $r>2$ remains open.

318308.title: The tropical Grassmannian containment conjecture for weighted trees
318308.literal_statement:
Let $m$ and $n$ be positive integers, let ${\mathcal{T}_{n}}$ denote the space of weighted trees on $n$ leaves, and let $phi^{(m)}$ be the map sending a dissimilarity vector to its $m$-dissimilarity vector. Let $\mathcal{G}_{m,n}$ denote the tropical Grassmannian.

**Weighted-tree tropical Grassmannian conjecture.** For $m\geq 5$, one has

$$
\phi^{(m)}({\mathcal{T}_{n}})\subset \mathcal{G}_{m,n}\cap \phi^{(m)}({\mathbb{R}}^{n\choose 2}).
$$

The theorem proved in the paper establishes the analogous containment for $m=4$; this conjecture proposes that it remains true for all higher $m$, although the paper does not resolve the question.

318494.title: Near-quadratic growth conjecture for similar copies in general position
318494.literal_statement:
Let $m\geq3$ be a positive integer and let $P$ be a finite pattern with no $m$ collinear points. For every real $\varepsilon>0$, there is $N(\varepsilon)>0$ such that for all $n\geq N(\varepsilon)$,

$$
S_{P}(n,m)\geq n^{2-\varepsilon}.
$$

**Near-quadratic growth conjecture.** The bound above should hold for every such $m$ and $P$. A proof cannot follow from the paper's main theorem and would require a different construction of sets in general position with many similar copies of $P$; the claim is presented as an expectation rather than an established result.

318543.title: Realizability conjecture for alternating independent-set numbers
318543.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $I(G;x)$ denote its independence polynomial, and let $\varphi(G)$ denote its decycling number. For a positive integer $k$ and an integer $q$, consider the values of $I(G;-1)$ for graphs whose decycling number is $k$.

**Realizability conjecture.** For every positive integer $k$ and each integer $q$ such that $|q|\leq 2^k$, there is a graph $G$ with $\varphi(G)=k$ and $I(G;-1)=q$.

The preceding theorem proves the upper bound $|I(G;-1)|\leq 2^{\varphi(G)}$, and disjoint unions of triangles attain the extreme magnitude. The conjecture asks whether every integer in the permitted range is realized for each positive decycling number.

318853.title: Conjecture on admissible pictures and Littlewood–Richardson crystals
318853.literal_statement:
Let $\lambda$, $\mu$, and $
u$ be Young diagrams with $|\lambda|+|\mu|=|
u|$. Let $A$ be an admissible order on the skew Young diagram $
u\setminus\lambda$, and let $A'$ be an admissible order on $\mu$. Write $\mathbf{P}(\mu,
u\setminus\lambda;A,A')$ for the set of admissible pictures and $\mathbf{B}(\mu)^

$$
\Psi:\mathbf{B}(\mu)^
u_\lambda[A']\longrightarrow \mathbf{P}(\mu,
u\setminus\lambda;A,A').
$$

This conjecture seeks to generalize the known correspondence between ordinary pictures and Littlewood–Richardson crystals to arbitrary admissible orders. Its status is not determined by the supplied source context.

318874.title: The regular oriented graph Hamilton decomposition conjecture above the $3/8$ threshold
318874.literal_statement: For $\gamma>0$, let $n_0=n_0(\gamma)$ be a threshold. An **$r$-regular oriented graph** on $n$ vertices is an oriented graph in which every vertex has indegree and outdegree $r$. **The conjecture.** For every $\gamma>0$ there exists $n_0=n_0(\gamma)$ such that, for all $n\geq n_0$ and all $r\geq(3/8+\gamma)n$, every $r$-regular oriented graph on $n$ vertices has a decomposition into Hamilton cycles. This would significantly generalize Kelly's conjecture. The source proves an approximate result for almost-regular oriented graphs with semidegree above $(3/8+\gamma)n$, while the exact decomposition statement remains open there.

318877.title: The affine-stratification conjecture for lattice games
318877.literal_statement:
A **lattice game** is a game played on a set of lattice points in a polyhedron, with a finite compatible rule set determining its winning and losing positions. Let $\mathcal{P}$ denote the set of P-positions. An **affine stratification** is a partition

$$
\mathcal{P}=\biguplus_{i=1}^r W_i
$$

where each $W_i$ is a finitely generated module for an affine semigroup $A_i\subset\mathbb{Z}^d$; explicitly, $W_i=F_i+A_i$ for a finite set $F_i\subset\mathbb{Z}^d$.

**Affine-stratification conjecture.** Every lattice game possesses an affine stratification.

Affine stratifications capture regular decompositions observed in examples, including normal-play squarefree games, but the conjecture remains unproved for arbitrary lattice games.

318976.title: Divisibility by six conjecture for realized permutations
318976.literal_statement:
Let $a_{n,N}$ denote the number defined in the paper for permutations of length $n$ realized by the shift on an $N$-letter alphabet, with $n,N\geq 3$.

**Divisibility by six conjecture.** For every $n,N\geq 3$, $a_{n,N}$ is divisible by $6$.

The paper presents this as a striking empirical property of the computed values. Although an explicit formula for $a_{n,N}$ is available, the source says that this divisibility is not apparent from the formula and leaves the general assertion as a conjecture.
